jobs.title: Sr. Robotic Software Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who We Are:

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military operators, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate, small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we've opened a Detroit manufacturing hub and we field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role and Your Impact:

We need a Senior Robotic Software Engineer who's a true workhorse on the Archimedes robotics stack. You write real production C++ across tracking, control and autonomy, and you raise the bar on how we ship. You'll work directly alongside our engineering leadersgup, owning features end to end while championing the QA and CI/CD practices that keep fielded software reliable. You're the senior IC who writes the code, makes it fast, then makes sure it survives contact with the field.

What You'll Own:

  • Hands-on C++ development across the stack, from raw sensor data through tracking, control and autonomy

  • Threading, process structure, performance and timing analysis on the paths you own

  • QA practices and test coverage alongside Erick and the Principal, built into how the team works, not bolted on

  • CI/CD and deployment hygiene for robotics and hardware-in-the-loop

  • Automated tests and tooling that catch failures before the range does

  • Code review and raising the quality bar across the robotics SWE team

  • Cross-functional work with controls, embedded and EE

What We're Looking For:

  • 4+ years writing production software with real shipped systems behind you

  • Strong production C++ (our core stack is C++, Python is tooling)

  • Real-time and performance chops: concurrency, profiling, latency and timing analysis

  • Experience building or operating CI/CD for robotics, hardware-in-the-loop or other hardware-facing systems

  • A genuine ownership mentality toward quality. You've seen what bad test discipline costs in the field and you fix it without being asked

Where you probably come from: Robotics companies that shipped to customers or operators, defense robotics, AV, aerospace, F1 or high-performance automotive, maritime, embedded or low-level systems work. Domain matters less than shipping.

We want to talk if: You're the engineer who writes the feature and the test for it, profiles it when it's slow, and quietly fixes the CI pipeline everyone else complains about. You've taken software from "works on my machine" to "works in the field."

Not a fit if: Your background is web, backend or full stack, you're a QA specialist who doesn't write production code, you're a researcher who hasn't shipped, or you think test discipline is someone else's job.

Nice to Haves:

  • ROS2

  • Rust or other systems languages

  • Motion planning, trajectory optimization, state estimation or sensor fusion

  • Defense or safety-critical software release experience

  • Built test automation frameworks for robotics or hardware-in-the-loop

Education: BS, MS or PhD in CS, EE, Robotics or equivalent. Track record matters more than degree.

How You Operate:

  • Extreme bias for action. You ship working code on real hardware, not slideware

  • You debug from first principles, not intuition alone

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration in a startup environment

  • Clear communicator across software, hardware, and operator-facing surfaces Self directed.

  • You identify what needs to happen next and do it without being told

Why Join Aurelius Systems?

  • Build more in 1 month than most people build in 1 year. We field test weekly. Your work makes the whole team faster.

  • Career velocity is real. With no middle management, there are no layers between you and impact.

  • Work on a problem that actually matters. Small cheap drones are changing warfare. Our laser systems are the asymmetric answer — infinite magazine, near zero cost per shot, scalable to every base, border, facility, and truck.

  • Join the densest defense startup ecosystem in the country. California is where the next generation of defense companies are being built.

How We Work:

Core hours are Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. When we're sprinting toward a demo or field test, the team ramps up — nights, weekends, whatever it takes to ship. When the sprint lands, we ramp down. We don't manufacture intensity for show.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary + equity

  • United Health Care medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Flexible 18 days PTO + 5 sick days

  • Travel to field test events and range days

  • Covered daily lunches and office snacks + drinks

  • E-bike / scooter stipend (Up to $500)

  • Direct access to leadership and real ownership over your work

 

Export Control Notice:

This role requires access to export-controlled information or items that require "U.S. Person" status. As defined by U.S. law, individuals who are any one of the following are considered to be a "U.S. Person": (1) U.S. citizens, (2) legal permanent residents (a.k.a. green card holders), and (3) certain protected classes of asylees and refugees, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

jobs.title: General Interest - Talent Network
jobs.descriptionHtml:
This Isn't a Catch-All Application:

If your background fits one of our open roles... apply there. Those postings exist for a reason and you'll get evaluated faster through the right pipeline.

This page is for people who don't see their exact role listed but belong at Aurelius. We're building a short list of people we want to pull from when new roles open, when we spin up internships, or when the right person shows up before the req does.

We review every submission. If you're not a fit, you'll know. If you are, you'll hear from us — maybe this month, maybe in six.

Who We're Looking For

You probably fall into one of these lanes:

1. Engineers Who Build Things

You're an ME, integration engineer, systems engineer, controls engineer, or something adjacent — and you've actually built software, or hardware that went into the real world. Maybe you worked on power systems at a FSAE Electric team and went pro. Maybe you've been at a defense startup or eVTOL company where you owned a subsystem end to end. Maybe you're still in school but you've built more in your garage or lab than most people build in their first three years of work.

We care about what you've built, not where you went to school.

2. Veterans With Technical or Operational Depth

You served and you're looking to stay in the fight from the builder side. Maybe you were a combat engineer, Special Operations, EOD, fire controlman, or had a technical MOS/rate. Maybe you ran operations or logistics in environments where things had to work the first time. We value military discipline and bias for action, but we're not collecting DD-214s — we need people who can contribute technically or operationally from day one.

3. Defense Business Operations

Proposal managers, capture managers, contract administrators, or BD professionals who have actually won contracts with Army, Navy, Marines, or MDA. Not people who worked at a prime and attended reviews. People who wrote the winning sections, managed the compliance matrix, or ran a capture from qualification to award. IDIQ and OTA experience is a plus. If you've only worked commercial or big-company BD where a team of 40 touches a single proposal, we're probably not the right fit.

4. Technical Operators

Growth, strategy, talent, mission operations — whatever you call it, you're the person who makes a small team punch way above its weight. Maybe you've scaled hiring at a defense startup and actually know the difference between a power electronics engineer and a semiconductor process engineer. Maybe you've run field operations, managed test campaigns, or built the operational backbone that lets engineers focus on engineering. Maybe you're a strategy or growth person who's worked in deep tech and understands long DoD sales cycles, IDIQ task orders, and what it takes to go from prototype to program of record. We don't need generalists who "wear many hats." We need people who've operated in high-output, resource-constrained environments and made things move faster than they had any right to.

What's True Across All of These

  • U.S. citizenship required. We work on classified programs and every role requires the ability to obtain a security clearance.

  • You'll be in San Francisco or Detroit. We're not remote. The hardware is here and so are you.

  • Bias for action over credentials. We've hired people without degrees who outperform PhDs. We've also hired PhDs who get their hands dirty. What matters is whether you build things or talk about building things.

  • Startup pace is real. Core hours are Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. When we sprint toward a demo or field test, the team goes hard — nights, weekends, whatever it takes. When the sprint lands, we recover. If that sounds like a warning, this isn't for you. If it sounds like home, keep reading.

What to Include in Your Application

Don't send a generic resume and cover letter. We read these and generic applications go to the bottom.

Instead, tell us:

  1. Which lane above fits you best and why you think you'd be a fit at Aurelius specifically — not just any defense startup.

  2. The hardest thing you've built or shipped. What was it, what was your role, and what made it hard?

  3. Your resume or LinkedIn — but only after #1 and #2. Those matter more.

If you're not sure whether to apply here or to a specific role, apply to the specific role. This page is for the people who know they belong here but don't see their exact seat yet.

jobs.title: Sr. Robotic Engineer, Controls
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who We Are:

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military operators, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing.

That's how we operate — small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we’ve opened a Detroit manufacturing hub and we field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role & Your Impact:

You'll own the precision motion stack, full stop.

The critical gap we're hiring for is a hands-on robotics controls engineer who can iterate fast on real hardware. Someone who can take a model, get it on the hardware, characterize what's actually happening, and tighten the loop. You think in Bode plots and step responses.

This is a senior IC role on the controls side. You'll own the architecture and tuning of the precision pointing and tracking control loops, the state estimation behind them, and the closed loop integration with the tracker.

What You'll Own:

  • Architecture and tuning of the precision pointing and tracking control loops

  • Closed loop tracking from sensor input through actuator command at hundreds of Hz

  • State estimation across IMU, encoder, and vision based feedback (Kalman filters, complementary filters, sensor fusion)

  • System identification and modeling of the gimbal, mount, and actuator dynamics

  • Actuator tuning, gain scheduling, and compensation for nonlinearities (backlash, friction, saturation)

  • Resonance characterization, notch filtering, and structural compensation

  • Simulation infrastructure for controls development

  • Hardware-in-the-loop test infrastructure for controls validation

  • Field characterization of the system against real targets at the range

  • Author controls documentation and tuning standards

What We're Looking For:

  • 4+ years of experience in robotics

  • Strong knowledge of fundamentals: classical controls, state space, LQR, MPC

  • Proven simulation experience and a track record of managing the sim-to-real gap on actual hardware

  • Modern C++ for real time control implementation

  • Python or MATLAB/Simulink for modeling, system ID, and analysis

  • State estimation in practice (Kalman, EKF, UKF, complementary filters)

  • System identification and frequency domain tuning

  • Direct experience with motion control hardware — servo drives, brushless motors, encoders, IMUs

  • Comfortable working at the seam between mechanical, electrical, and software

  • Understanding of latency, jitter, and how they kill control loop performance

Not a fit if: Your controls experience is purely simulation, your real world tuning amounts to changing PID gains in a UI, or you've never had to characterize a resonance, model an actuator, or fight a sensor that lies to you. We need someone who's tuned hardware that fought back.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Advanced MPC — nonlinear MPC, robust MPC, or real-time NMPC on resource constrained hardware

  • Gimbal, beam director, or precision pointing system experience

Education:

  • Operate comfortably with ambiguity and fast iteration in a growing defense technology company

  • Make sound decisions using program facts, cost and schedule data, and customer priorities

  • Communicate clearly with customers, engineering, operations, partners, and executive leadership

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate: small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we opened a Detroit manufacturing hub and field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role & Your Impact

We need a Principal Controls Engineer who owns the math behind putting a laser on a drone and keeping it there.

You'll own beam control and tracking as a theory domain across the whole system: the nested coarse and fine pointing architecture, the estimators that fuse radar cues, EO/IR track and inertial data, the jitter and latency budgets, and the analysis that says what the system can and cannot hit before we drive to the range to find out. You'll partner with the perception, optics and mechanical leads on architecture and roadmap, and you'll be the senior technical voice on controls decisions inside the company.

You'll derive the loop, run it in our in-house simulator, and have it on the hardware in days, not weeks. Then you'll stand on our outdoor range, control and refine laser positioning yourself, and watch it hold microradian precision on a maneuvering drone.

What You'll Own

  • Control architecture for the beam director: coarse gimbal and fine steering mirror loop structure, bandwidth allocation, multi-rate design, and the handoff between stages

  • Target state estimation: Kalman, IMM and nonlinear filters that fuse radar cue, EO/IR track and inertial data into a predicted aimpoint, with latency compensation designed in, not patched on

  • Line-of-sight stabilization and jitter rejection: inertial stabilization, accelerometer feedforward, notch and adaptive filtering for structural modes, and the control-structure interaction analysis behind them

  • The pointing error budget and the field result: jitter, bias, latency and atmospheric terms allocated across the system, then microradian pointing precision achieved and held on our outdoor range against dynamic, real-world targets through hands-on experimentation and deployment

  • Plant modeling and system identification: frequency-domain and time-domain ID of gimbal, mirror and structure, hardware-in-the-loop validation, and the models our in-house simulators run on

  • Robustness and stability analysis: margins, sensitivity, worst-case disturbance and parameter variation, with the proof, not just the Bode plot

  • Fire control integration: cue to track to engage handoff, engagement sequencing, dwell and aimpoint maintenance logic, and safety interlocks with the laser team

  • Rapid iteration from simulator to hardware: control algorithms out of the sim and onto the system in days, kHz-rate loops on embedded targets with the software team, and the test campaign that shows field data matches the prediction

  • Technical review and risk: catching what others miss in controls, estimation and sensor integration across the system

  • Mentorship by example. Engineers learn from watching you work, not from being managed by you

What We're Looking For

  • PhD-level depth in control theory and estimation. You can derive and defend the architecture, not just tune it: robust control (H-infinity, mu-synthesis, LQG), optimal estimation (Kalman variants, IMM, nonlinear observers), multi-rate and sampled-data design, adaptive and learning-based disturbance rejection

  • 10+ years closing loops on precision pointing, tracking or stabilization hardware, PhD research included, on systems that had to meet a measured spec in the field

  • Microradian-class line-of-sight work: beam directors, fine steering mirrors, gimbaled EO/IR sensors, laser comm pointing-acquisition-tracking terminals, telescope or spacecraft pointing, or precision mechatronics at equivalent precision

  • Hands-on system identification and plant modeling against real structural dynamics, and a record of models that predicted what the hardware then did

  • Real-time implementation chops. You've shipped loops in C or C++ on embedded or RTOS targets, or worked tightly with the engineers who did, and you know what latency and quantization do to your margins

  • Comfort being the technical anchor for controls on a small team, not the manager of a large one

Where you probably come from: Directed energy or beam control programs at primes and government labs (AFRL, MIT Lincoln Lab, NRL, APL, Sandia), laser communications terminal teams, EO/IR gimbal and stabilized-sensor houses, telescope or spacecraft precision pointing, adaptive optics groups, or a controls PhD group that transitioned its work onto real hardware.

We want to talk if: You've owned the jitter budget on a pointing system, held microradian precision in the field against moving targets, and the data matched your prediction. Your dissertation was in estimation, robust or adaptive control and you've since put that math on hardware that shipped. You can write the proof and the C++ in the same week.

Not a fit if: Your controls experience is PID tuning from a block library without the theory to say why it works. You're a theorist who has never closed a loop on real hardware, or a manager without recent hands-on work.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Directed energy weapon or high energy laser program experience

  • Adaptive optics: wavefront sensing, deformable mirror control, turbulence modeling (Greenwood frequency, tilt statistics)

  • Atmospheric propagation and beam wander modeling

  • MATLAB/Simulink to production code generation, or Python and C++ toolchains for control design and hardware-in-the-loop

  • Publications or patents in control, estimation or precision pointing

  • Founder or founding engineer background at a hardware company

  • Familiarity with MIL-STD standards and ITAR compliance

  • Active security clearance or ability to obtain one

Education

PhD in Control Systems, Electrical, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Applied Math, or a related field, with a dissertation in control or estimation theory. An MS plus a research-grade record of theory work put on fielded hardware can substitute.

How You Operate

  • Extreme bias for action. You'd rather prove the margin and test it this week than model it for a quarter

  • You characterize your own systems before the field does

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration in a startup environment

  • You debug from first principles. When the field data disagrees with the model, you find out which one is wrong

  • Clear communicator across optics, mechanical, software, perception and ML teams, including explaining the math to people who don't have it

  • Self directed. You identify what needs to happen next and do it without being told

Why Join Aurelius Systems

  • Build more in 1 month than most engineers build in 1 year. We field test weekly. Your work goes downrange, not into a filing cabinet.

  • Career velocity is real. At ~15 engineers, there are no layers between you and impact.

  • Work on a problem that actually matters. Small cheap drones are changing warfare. Our laser systems are the asymmetric answer: infinite magazine, near zero cost per shot, scalable to every base, border, facility, and truck.

  • Join the densest defense startup ecosystem in the country. California is where the next generation of defense companies are being built.

How We Work

Core hours are Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. When we're sprinting toward a demo or field test, the team ramps up: nights, weekends, whatever it takes to ship. When the sprint lands, we ramp down. We don't manufacture intensity for show.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Covered daily lunches and office snacks and drinks
